sections.heading: Why the Korean Folk Village Is K-Drama's Favorite Joseon Set
paragraphs: The Korean Folk Village (한국민속촌, Hanguk Minsokchon) in Giheung-gu, Yongin, is an open-air museum and theme park that recreates life in the late Joseon Dynasty. Opened in 1974, it gathers farmhouses, a market street, a yangban (aristocrat) estate, a local government office, a Confucian school, shrines, mills and workshops from different regions of Korea into one walkable village, with a stream and wooden bridges running through the middle.

For drama producers, that makes it a ready-made Joseon town with no power lines, apartment blocks or neon signs in the frame, and only about an hour from Seoul. Korea's public KCISA filming-location dataset (한국문화정보원 미디어 촬영지 데이터, published via 공공데이터포털) lists 15 records at the Korean Folk Village (경기도 용인시 기흥구 민속촌로 90): 9 dramas, 1 film and 5 K-pop artist entries. Many sageuk fans will recognize one spot in particular, the village's wooden bridge, which four different dramas in the dataset use.

This guide covers only the Korean Folk Village: which scenes the public data places here, what to look for as you walk, the exact Korean address for a taxi, how to get there by bus or subway from Seoul and Suwon, where to eat, and tips for a smooth visit.

sections.heading: What Was Filmed at the Korean Folk Village (Public Data)
paragraphs: Everything below comes from the KCISA records for 한국민속촌. Where a record is short or vague, we only repeat what it says and do not add scene details we cannot verify.

The village's wooden bridge (나무다리) is the most-repeated location in the dataset. In 100 Days My Prince (백일의 낭군님), it is the bridge where Hong-shim (Nam Ji-hyun) waits for her brother once a month, keeping a promise they made ten years earlier. The record adds that in episode 2 this is where Jeong Je-yoon (Kim Seon-ho) and the adult Lee Yul (D.O. of EXO) first see Hong-shim, and that in episode 5 Je-yoon prepares the floating lanterns that make her wish come true.

In The King's Affection (연모), episode 1, the young Jung Ji-woon (Go Woo-rim) waits on the wooden bridge for the young Dam-i (Choi Myung-bin), as they had arranged, but she never comes. In Arang and the Magistrate (아랑사또전), episode 2, an irritated and frustrated Arang (Shin Min-a) crosses the same bridge, and in The Crowned Clown (왕이 된 남자), episode 1, Ha-seon (Yeo Jin-goo) and his troupe of performers leap across it.

Tale of the Nine-Tailed (구미호뎐) brings the bridge into the present day. In episode 5, Lee Yeon (Lee Dong-wook) and Nam Ji-ah (Jo Bo-ah) visit the folk village together. Ji-ah sees a hanbok in a shop and decides to wear it, and when Lee Yeon finds her in it he is pulled straight back into his memories of A-eum. He spots her on the wooden bridge and runs to kiss her.

The village has also stood in for ordinary Joseon towns in harder times. In Dae Jang Geum (대장금, also known as Jewel in the Palace), Jang-geum (Lee Young-ae) cares for smallpox patients in this village in episode 51, and in episode 54 she gives birth to Min Jeong-ho's (Ji Jin-hee) child here. In Iljimae (일지매), the dataset says the village was used to film a settlement struck by an epidemic.

The Netflix series Kingdom (킹덤) is also listed, with the record simply describing the Korean Folk Village as a representative traditional-culture theme park and a Kingdom filming location. For Hwarang (화랑), the record notes a scene of Choi Min-ho's character talking with his younger sibling.
The only film in the dataset is Masquerade (광해, 왕이 된 남자, 2012), where the record notes the spot where Lee Byung-hun's character is flogged (곤장).

Five artist entries round out the list. Kang Daniel visited in episode 5 of his travel log series, Stray Kids filmed episode 5 of Finding SKZ here, Apink's Bomi and Hayoung came to the park, Dreamcatcher's Dami visited, and g.o.d's Park Joon-hyung stopped by for the web show Wassup Man. The dataset does not give the exact corners for these visits, so treat the whole village as fair game for recreating their photos.

sections.heading: Walking the Village: Bridge, Government Office and Yangban Estate
paragraphs: The village is large, and many visitors spend three to five hours here. A simple loop that covers the drama spots looks like this.

Follow the stream that runs through the middle of the village. This is where the bridge scenes from 100 Days My Prince, The King's Affection, Arang and the Magistrate, The Crowned Clown and Tale of the Nine-Tailed were shot. Look for a simple wooden footbridge over the water framed by willows and thatched roofs; on a calm day you get a reflection that looks straight out of a sageuk opening scene.

The local magistrate's office, with its tiled gate, courtyard and raised hall, is the kind of set where Joseon trials and punishments play out. Fans of Masquerade and of magistrate dramas like Arang and the Magistrate will recognize the layout.

Thatched farmhouses from different provinces, including a Jeju-style lane with black stone walls, fill much of the village. Further in, the yangban estate shows how wealthy families lived, with tiled roofs, inner courtyards and pavilions. The market street is where the village feels most like a drama town, with low tile-roofed stalls and food counters.

The village runs traditional performances, such as farmers' music (nongak), tightrope walking and equestrian shows, and it often adds seasonal festivals and night events. Schedules change by season and day of the week, so check the timetable at the entrance or on the official site and plan your bridge photos around the show times when the crowds move to the arena.

sections.heading: Address, Hours and How to Get There
paragraphs: Show this to the driver or paste it into Naver Map, KakaoMap or Kakao T: 경기도 용인시 기흥구 민속촌로 90 (90 Minsokchon-ro, Giheung-gu, Yongin-si, Gyeonggi-do), or simply 한국민속촌. The phone number in the public data is 031-288-0000.

The KCISA data lists the village as open daily from 10:00 to 18:00. In practice the park adjusts its closing time and operating days by season and day of the week, and admission is paid, with prices that differ between weekdays, weekends and special events. Check the current hours and prices on the official website, koreanfolk.co.kr, before you set out.

The village's official transport guide lists three direct buses from Seoul: 5001-1 from Sinnonhyeon Station via Gangnam and Yangjae, 1560 from Gangnam Station (get off at 민속촌 입구, Folk Village Entrance), and 4101 from the Sungnyemun / Seoul Station area. From Incheon Airport, the airport bus A8877 also stops at the village. These are the easiest options if your hotel is near one of the starting points.

The nearest subway station is Sanggal Station (상갈역) on the Suin-Bundang Line. Leave by Exit 3 and take bus 37 or 10-5 to the Korean Folk Village stop. From Suwon Station (Line 1 and KTX), leave by Exit 4 and take bus 37 or 10-5. From Jukjeon Station on the Suin-Bundang Line, bus 30 also runs to the village. A taxi from Sanggal Station is a short ride of roughly 10 minutes.

Return buses can be infrequent in the evening. Save the return stop in your map app and check the last bus on Naver Map or KakaoMap before the park closes, or plan to take a taxi back to Sanggal or Suwon Station.

sections.heading: Where to Eat Near the Korean Folk Village
paragraphs: Inside the village. The village market street (장터) is the classic lunch stop, with Korean snacks and simple meals such as savory pancakes (pajeon), rice soups and rice-cake treats served at low wooden tables. Eating here also makes for a very drama-like photo.

A samgyetang restaurant from public data. The KCISA dataset lists 이창노녹두삼계탕메기매운탕 민속촌본점, featured on SBS's Morning Wide (episode 7080) for its mung-bean samgyetang (ginseng chicken soup). It is about 1 km from the village at 경기도 용인시 기흥구 사은로 74 (보리마을), and the record lists it as open Tuesday to Sunday from 09:00 to 22:00 and closed on Mondays. Restaurant details can change, so confirm on Naver Map before going.

Make it a culture day. The Nam June Paik Art Center (백남준아트센터, 경기도 용인시 기흥구 백남준로 10) is about 1.5 km away and appears in the dataset for a visit by ATEEZ members Wooyoung, Seonghwa and Hongjoong. The public data lists it as open Tuesday to Sunday from 10:00 to 18:00 and closed on Mondays, New Year's Day and Lunar holidays. It pairs well with a morning at the folk village.

sections.heading: Visit Tips: Best Time, Photos and Etiquette
paragraphs: Arrive at opening. School groups and tour buses arrive mid-morning. If you want the wooden bridge without a crowd, head there first and save the market street and performances for later.

Seasons. Spring blossoms and autumn leaves (usually late October to early November) are the most photogenic, and the stream reflects the color beautifully. Summer is hot with little shade on the open lanes. Winter is cold, but snow on thatched roofs looks like a sageuk winter episode.

Wear (or rent) a hanbok. Like Nam Ji-ah in Tale of the Nine-Tailed, many visitors walk the village in hanbok. Check the official site or on-site signage for current rental options and any hanbok-related ticket offers before you go.
Plan a full day. Counting the bus or subway ride, a visit easily fills most of a day. Bring comfortable shoes, because the paths are mostly dirt and gravel.

Respect the place. The houses are part of a museum: do not climb walls or roofs, stay out of roped-off rooms, ask before photographing performers and staff up close, and keep drones grounded unless you have permission.

sections.heading: Why Dumulmeori Is a Favorite K-Drama Riverside
paragraphs: Dumulmeori (두물머리) means "the head of two waters". It is the spit of land in Yangseo-myeon, Yangpyeong-gun, Gyeonggi-do, where the North Han River (북한강) and the South Han River (남한강) meet and become the Han River that flows on through Seoul. Once a busy ferry landing where boats from upriver unloaded timber and goods for the capital, it is now a free riverside park with a huge old zelkova tree, lotus beds, a red-sailed traditional boat, and a wide, calm stretch of water framed by low mountains.

That calm water, the soft morning mist and the sense of being far from the city, while sitting only about an hour from central Seoul by train, make it a natural set for walks, confessions and farewells. Korea's public KCISA filming-location dataset (한국문화정보원 미디어 촬영지 데이터, published via 공공데이터포털) lists 20 records at Dumulmeori itself: 17 drama entries covering 15 different dramas, 1 film and 2 K-pop artist entries. Four more records belong to a TV-famous lotus-leaf hot dog stand and a rice-cake restaurant on the same road.

This guide covers only Dumulmeori: which scenes the public data places here, what to see on the riverbank, the exact Korean address for a taxi, how to get there from Seoul on the Gyeongui-Jungang Line, where to eat, and when to go for the famous mist.

sections.heading: What Was Filmed at Dumulmeori (Public Data)
paragraphs: Everything below comes from the KCISA records for 두물머리 and 양평 두물머리 (경기도 양평군 양서면 양수리 / 두물머리길). Where a record is short or vague, we only repeat what it says and do not add scene details we cannot verify.

The best-known record is She Was Pretty (그녀는 예뻤다), which has two entries. In episodes 13 and 14, after a picnic, Ji Sung-joon (Park Seo-joon) confesses his everlasting love to Kim Hye-jin (Hwang Jung-eum) here, and the dataset separately describes Dumulmeori as the location of the couple's kiss scene. In Goddess of Marriage (결혼의 여신), episode 4, Song Ji-hye (Nam Sang-mi) and Kang Tae-wook (Kim Ji-hoon) stroll along the river while getting to know each other, and in First Love (첫사랑), the 1990s classic, Sung Chan-hyuk (Choi Soo-jong) and Lee Seung-yeon (Lee Hyo-jung) come here on a date in episode 23.

In the final scene of episode 16 of Sweet Stranger and Me (우리집에 사는 남자), Hong Na-ri (Soo Ae) and Go Nan-gil (Kim Young-kwang) walk away hand in hand along the riverbank. Discovery of Love (연애의 발견) also lists Dumulmeori as a place Jung Yu-mi and Eric Mun's characters visit, and Let's Eat 3 (식샤를 합시다 3) used it as a scenic stop.

In episode 21 of My Love from the Star (별에서 온 그대), crowds gather in this riverside park to watch the meteor shower, with stars flying across the sky like UFOs. The Beauty Inside (뷰티 인사이드) has two entries: in episode 9, Han Se-gye (Seo Hyun-jin) undergoes a shaman's gut ritual here while her best friend Yoo Woo-mi (Moon Ji-in) and Ryu Eun-ho (Ahn Jae-hyun) watch, and another record notes Lee Min-ki and others talking on a bench.

Several dramas use the river for heavier moments. In Two Cops (투깝스), episode 20, Cha Dong-tak (Jo Jung-suk) comes here to say goodbye to his best friend Lee Doo-sik, killed in prison. In Graceful Family (우아한 가), episode 16, the family pays final respects to Mo Wan-soo (Lee Kyu-han), whose resting place is here in the story. In Undercover (언더커버), episode 16, Han Jung-hyun (Ji Jin-hee) and Choi Yeon-soo (Kim Hyun-joo) visit together.

In Melting Me Softly (날 녹여주오), episode 8, producer Ma Dong-chan (Ji Chang-wook) scouts the park as a filming location. In When I Was the Most Beautiful (내가 가장 예뻤을 때), episode 1, art teacher Oh Ye-ji (Im Soo-hyang) brings her class here for an outdoor drawing lesson. Bride of the Century (백년의 신부) episode 2 has Choi Il-do (Choi Il-hwa) come here thinking of a woman in a wedding dress, and in Golden Bride (황금신부) episode 4, Kang Woo-nam (Kang Shin-il) brings his son and Jinju Nguyen (Lee Young-ah) here the day before their arranged wedding.

The 2016 comedy film Luck-Key (럭키) used Dumulmeori as a natural backdrop. On the K-pop side, the dataset lists NU'EST, after Minhyun visited Yangpyeong with his mother on I Live Alone (나 혼자 산다), and TWICE, who planted rice here on the KBS show 6시 내고향.

sections.heading: Walking Dumulmeori: The Point, the Frame and the Lotus Paths
paragraphs: Dumulmeori is compact. A relaxed loop of the riverbank takes 45 to 90 minutes, longer if you continue across the pontoon bridge to Semiwon. The paths are flat and mostly unpaved, so it is easy walking for all ages.

At the tip of the spit stands a giant zelkova tree that local tourism sources describe as more than 400 years old, once a landmark for boatmen. Nearby, a wooden boat with a reddish-brown sail (황포돛배) is moored as a reminder of the old ferry days. These two, with the water behind them, are the image most dramas reach for.
A large wooden picture frame stands on the riverbank so you can "frame" the river and mountains. Expect a short queue on weekend afternoons; early morning is much quieter.

Lotus beds line the shallow water near the point. They bloom in midsummer, but even in autumn the dried leaves and reflections are photogenic. A path follows the water past benches like the one in The Beauty Inside record, then continues to the Baedari pontoon bridge (배다리), a recreation of the boat bridge used in the Joseon era, which crosses to the Semiwon (세미원) water garden. Dumulmeori is free; Semiwon charges admission and keeps its own hours.

sections.heading: Address, Hours and How to Get There
paragraphs: The simplest option is to show the driver 두물머리. The KCISA records list the location as 경기도 양평군 양서면 양수리 and 경기도 양평군 양서면 두물머리길. Typing 두물머리 into Naver Map, KakaoMap or Kakao T brings up the right place and its parking lot. From Yangsu Station, a taxi takes about 5 minutes.

According to the public data, Dumulmeori is open 24 hours a day, every day of the year (매일 00시 - 24시, 연중무휴). It is an open riverside area with no admission fee. The phone number in the record is 031-775-8700, the local tourist information line (Korean). Parking is available nearby, but lots fill up on weekends and fees may apply.

Take the Gyeongui-Jungang Line (경의중앙선) toward Yongmun or Jipyeong and get off at Yangsu Station (양수역). From Cheongnyangni or Wangsimni it takes roughly 45 to 60 minutes, and the fare works with T-money. Some trains turn back before Yangsu, so check the destination on the platform board. From the station, walking to Dumulmeori takes about 25 to 30 minutes on flat roads and riverside paths. Use Naver Map or KakaoMap for walking directions, because Google Maps does not give full walking routes in Korea.

A popular alternative is to walk about 10 to 15 minutes from Yangsu Station to Semiwon (세미원, 양수로 93), go through the garden, and cross the Baedari pontoon bridge to Dumulmeori. Semiwon has an admission fee and, according to its official information, closes on Mondays from November to March; the bridge can also close in bad weather or high water. Check before you go.

Yangsu-ri sits on the Namhangang bike path. Riders often cross the old North Han River Railway Bridge (북한강철교), now a walking and cycling bridge next to Yangsu Station. The KCISA data notes that Park Shin-hye and Kim Rae-won's characters ride bikes across it in episode 2 of Doctors (닥터스).

sections.heading: Where to Eat and Drink Near Dumulmeori
paragraphs: The KCISA dataset also lists TV-featured snacks and restaurants in Yangseo-myeon. Hours below come from the public data and may have changed, so check Naver Map before you go.

The snack everyone buys is the lotus-leaf hot dog at Dumulmeori Yeon Hot Dog (두물머리연핫도그, 양서면 두물머리길 103-8), a stand on the road to the point. The data lists it on 2TV Saengsaeng Information, Omniscient Interfering View (전지적 참견시점, ep. 43) and MBC Power Magazine, open daily 10am to 6pm. Next door, Narutoga (나루터가, 두물머리길 101) appeared on VJ Special Forces for its rice cakes and is listed as open daily 10:30am to 8pm.

For a meal near Yangsu Station, the dataset includes Somunnan Yeon Kalguksu (소문난연칼국수, 양수로152번길 2-1), featured on Amazing Saturday for lotus-leaf noodle soup, and Dumulgil Hanjeongsik (두물길한정식, 양수로 111 2층), featured on the same show for marinated crab set meals. Both are listed as open daily 10am to 8:30pm. Yangsu Garden (양수가든, 북한강로 4), an eel restaurant, appeared on Welcome, First Time in Korea? (어서와 한국은 처음이지) and closes on Tuesdays.
For coffee, Susu Cafe (수수 카페, 북한강로89번길 16) is where NU'EST's Minhyun took his mother on I Live Alone, listed as open 10am to 10pm.

sections.heading: Visit Tips: Best Time, Photos and Etiquette
paragraphs: Come at dawn for the mist. Dumulmeori is famous for the morning fog (물안개) that rises off the water, especially on cool, still mornings in spring and autumn. Photographers arrive before sunrise. The earliest trains will not always get you there in time, so a nearby stay or a taxi helps.
Sunset works too. If you cannot make dawn, late afternoon light on the water and the zelkova is lovely, and the riverbank is calmer after the day-trip crowds leave.

Seasons. Lotus blooms peak in July and August (Semiwon holds a lotus festival in summer). Autumn leaves turn in late October to early November. Winter is cold and windy by the water, but snow on the riverbank is beautiful.
Avoid weekend afternoons if you can. The photo frame and the hot dog stand get long lines, and parking fills up. Weekday mornings are the quietest.

Respect the place. Stay on the paths around the lotus beds, do not climb the old tree or the boat, keep drones grounded unless you have checked local rules, and take your trash with you. Yangsu-ri is a living village, so keep noise down near homes.

sections.heading: Why Naksan Park Is One of Seoul's Most Filmed Viewpoints
paragraphs: Naksan Park (낙산공원) sits on Naksan, a low hill on the eastern edge of old Seoul in Jongno-gu, right above the theater district of Daehangno. The name means "camel mountain", because the hill was said to look like a camel's hump. Its ridge carries one of the best-preserved stretches of the Seoul City Wall (한양도성), the stone fortress wall that surrounded the Joseon capital, and from the top you look across rooftops to Bukhansan, Namsan Tower and the towers of Dongdaemun.

That combination of an old stone wall, a free park open around the clock, and a wide night view is exactly what Korean location managers want for a quiet conversation, a confession or a late-night walk. Korea's public KCISA filming-location dataset (한국문화정보원 미디어 촬영지 데이터) lists 29 records at the Naksan Park address (낙산길 41): 25 TV dramas, 2 films, 1 variety show and 1 artist entry. Four more records sit on the Naksan Fortress West Road (낙산성곽서길), the wall-side path that leads up to the park from Ihwa-dong.

This guide covers only Naksan Park: which scenes the public data places here, how to walk up from Hyehwa or Dongdaemun, the exact Korean address for a taxi, food and cafes nearby, and when the view is at its best.

sections.heading: What Was Filmed at Naksan Park (Public Data)
paragraphs: Everything below comes from the KCISA records for 낙산공원 (서울특별시 종로구 낙산길 41) and 낙산성곽서길. Where a record is vague, we kept only what it says.

My Mister (나의 아저씨) is the record many fans look for: in episode 5, this is where the grandmother is wheeled up in a cart so she can see the moon, one of the drama's gentlest scenes. In The King 2 Hearts (더킹 투하츠), episode 7, Princess Lee Jae-shin (Lee Yoon-ji) and royal guard Eun Si-kyung (Jo Jung-suk) sit on the fortress wall, make wishes on a shooting star, and he falls for her as she sings about first love.

Because This Is My First Life (이번 생은 처음이라) has three entries. In episode 7, Yeon Bok-nam (Kim Min-kyu) brings Yoon Ji-ho (Jung So-min) here by motorbike to show her the view, and they return in episode 8. In episode 9, Nam Se-hee (Lee Min-ki) runs up the Naksan Fortress West Road toward the park. Radio Romance (라디오 로맨스) episode 9 has Ji Soo-ho (Yoon Doo-joon) and Song Geu-rim (Kim So-hyun) talking about their families here before she finally hugs him, and in Let Me Hear Your Song (너의 노래를 들려줘) episode 4, Jang Yoon (Yeon Woo-jin) brings Hong I-young (Kim Se-jeong) to the park and asks if he can kiss her.

In the final episode 16 of Dae Jang Geum Is Watching (대장금이 보고 있다), Han San-hae (Shin Dong-wook) proposes to Bok Seung-ah (Kwon Yu-ri) here. Twelve Nights (열두밤) uses the park twice for Cha Hyun-oh (Shin Hyun-soo) and Han Yu-kyung (Han Seung-yeon) during their 2010 stay in Seoul, including the bench scene where she falls asleep on his shoulder. Run On (런온) episode 11 shows Ki Sun-gyeom (Im Si-wan) and Oh Mi-joo (Shin Se-kyung) walking up the park on an evening date, and in 18 Again (18 어게인) episode 1, young Hong Dae-young (Lee Do-hyun) and Jung Da-jung talk about what it means to become young parents.

The hill is also a favorite for daily-life scenes. Misaeng (미생) opens episode 8 with Jang Geu-rae (Im Si-wan) on a morning jog here, and in Today's Webtoon (오늘의 웹툰) On Ma-eum (Kim Se-jeong) trains by jogging in the park every morning. Strong Girl Bong-soon (힘쎈여자 도봉순) episode 7 shows Do Bong-soon (Park Bo-young) spending time with her mother and grandmother at the park playground. Should We Kiss First? (키스 먼저 할까요) episode 1 has Son Moo-han (Kam Woo-sung) walking his dog here to think creatively, and Rooftop Prince (옥탑방 왕세자) episode 12 has the characters resting on the fortress wall.

Other drama records include 365: Repeat the Year (Shin Ga-hyun, played by Nam Ji-hyun, comes to draw at night in episode 2), Can You Hear My Heart, Come Back Mister, Liar Game, Undercover, One Dollar Lawyer, Over the Rainbow, The Secret Life of My Secretary, Feast of the Gods, Pots of Gold and the weekend drama Beautiful Love, Wonderful Life. On the West Road, the data adds Brilliant Legacy (찬란한 유산), Touch (터치, 2020) and The Second Husband (두 번째 남편).

Two films are listed: Assassination (암살), with the record describing Naksan as one of Seoul's signature night-view spots used in the film, and Confidential Assignment (공조), where Yoo Hae-jin's character is caught in a lie. The dating show Heart Signal (하트시그널) filmed a walk here, and the dataset also tags singer-actor Rain (비) with a meeting scene at the park from one of his dramas.

sections.heading: Walking Naksan Park and the City Wall
paragraphs: Naksan Park is small, and most visitors spend 45 to 90 minutes walking the ridge. Paths are paved but steep in places, so wear comfortable shoes.

The top of the hill opens into a plaza with benches and a viewing area facing north and west. This is where most of the bench and conversation scenes feel like they were shot: the wall drops away below you and the mountains line the horizon.

A path runs along the inside of the Seoul City Wall for the whole length of the park. Walk it south and downhill and it continues to Heunginjimun (흥인지문, Dongdaemun Gate); walk it north and it leads toward Hyehwamun and Seongbuk-dong. You can also step through small gates to the outer side of the wall, where the stones look older and the view is less crowded. Please do not climb or sit on the wall in places where signs prohibit it, even if a drama character did.

The western slope below the park is Ihwa-dong (이화동), a hillside neighborhood known for its stairs and murals. The Naksan Fortress West Road (낙산성곽서길) climbs between the village and the wall, and it is the most scenic way up. Ihwa-dong is a residential area: keep your voice down, do not photograph people's homes or doors up close, and stay on public paths.

sections.heading: Address, Hours and How to Get There
paragraphs: Show the driver 낙산공원 or the address 서울특별시 종로구 낙산길 41. It works in Naver Map, KakaoMap and Kakao T. A taxi from Myeongdong or Insadong usually takes about 15 to 20 minutes, depending on traffic.

According to the public data, Naksan Park is open 24 hours a day, every day of the year (매일 00시 - 24시, 연중무휴). It is a public park, so there is no admission fee. The phone number listed is 02-743-7985.

Take Seoul Subway Line 4 to Hyehwa Station (혜화역) and leave by Exit 2. Walk through Marronnier Park and up through Ihwa-dong; it is about 15 minutes uphill on foot. Type 낙산공원 into Naver Map or KakaoMap for walking directions, since Google Maps does not give full walking routes in Korea.

If you would rather skip the climb, the green village bus Jongno 03 (종로03) runs from near Hyehwa Station up to a stop at the park entrance (낙산공원 정류장). Check the current route and stop in Naver Map before you go, because village bus routes are occasionally adjusted. Seoul village buses accept T-money and most contactless transit cards.

For a longer walk, start at Dongdaemun Station (동대문역), go to Heunginjimun Gate, and follow the city wall trail uphill. It takes roughly 20 to 30 minutes to reach the hilltop and is one of the easiest sections of the Seoul City Wall to walk.

sections.heading: Where to Eat and Drink Near Naksan Park
paragraphs: The KCISA dataset also lists TV-featured cafes and restaurants within a short walk. Hours below are from the public data and may have changed, so check Naver Map before you go.

Hakrim Coffee (학림, 종로구 대학로 119 2층) is a long-running Daehangno coffee house on the second floor across from Marronnier Park. The data lists it in My Love from the Star, The Heirs, Youth of May and Because This Is My First Life, listed as open daily 10am to 11pm. In Ihwa-dong, right below the park, Cafe Gaebbul (카페 개뿔, 종로구 낙산성곽서1길 26) appeared on I Live Alone, and Chaek Ingneun Goyangi (책읽는고양이, 낙산성곽서1길 18-2), a small coffee spot, was featured on 2TV Saengsaeng Information.

For a meal in Daehangno, Sundae Sillok (순대실록, 종로구 동숭길 127) is the Korean blood-sausage restaurant visited in Let's Eat 2, and Dodoya (도도야, 동숭길 39) is a Japanese kamameshi (pot rice) restaurant that the data notes as a regular haunt of director Park Chan-wook. On the east side of the hill, the cafe Tertre (테르트르, 종로구 낙산5길 46) was featured on You Quiz on the Block for its view over Changsin-dong.

sections.heading: Visit Tips: Best Time, Photos and Etiquette
paragraphs: Go at sunset and stay after dark. The wall faces west toward Bukhansan and Inwangsan, so the hour before sunset is the classic time. Once the lights come on along the wall path, you get the night view that the Assassination record describes and that so many drama confessions use.
Mornings for quiet. If you want the Misaeng and Today's Webtoon feeling, come early. You will share the path with local joggers and walkers rather than photo groups.

Seasons. Spring brings cherry and forsythia blossoms along the wall, and autumn leaves color the slopes in late October to early November. Winter evenings are cold and windy on the ridge; bring a layer even in spring and fall.
Combine it. Naksan Park pairs well with an afternoon show in Daehangno, or with Dongdaemun Design Plaza and the Dongdaemun markets after you walk down the wall to Heunginjimun.

Respect the heritage. The Seoul City Wall is a national historic site. Follow signs about where you may stand, keep tripods off narrow paths, take your trash with you, and keep noise low near the homes of Ihwa-dong, especially at night.

sections.heading: Why Gwanghallu Garden Is Korea's Favorite Joseon Palace Stand-In
paragraphs: Gwanghallu Garden (광한루원) in Namwon, North Jeolla, is one of the most famous traditional gardens in Korea. Its centerpiece, Gwanghallu Pavilion, is a red-pillared Joseon-era pavilion that is designated a national Treasure. Around it, a large pond holds small islands, a four-arched stone bridge and a second pavilion on stilts. The garden is also the setting of Chunhyangjeon (The Tale of Chunhyang), Korea's best-known love story, in which Chunhyang and Lee Mong-ryong first meet here on the day of the Dano festival.

That mix of water, old wood and stone makes the garden look like a royal palace on screen, even though it is a provincial site several hours south of Seoul. Korea's public KCISA filming-location dataset (한국문화정보원 미디어 촬영지 데이터) lists 17 separate records at this one address: 15 TV dramas, one film and one K-pop variety show. Several of the biggest historical dramas of the last 15 years used the garden as part of the palace, which is why many visitors recognize it before they know its name.

This guide covers only Gwanghallu Garden: what was filmed where according to the public data, how to get there from Seoul, the exact Korean address for a taxi, where to eat nearby, and how to time your visit.

sections.heading: What Was Filmed at Gwanghallu Garden (Public Data)
paragraphs: Everything in this section comes from the KCISA records for 광한루원 (요천로 1447). Where a record is unclear or looks garbled, we left out the detail rather than guess.

Love in the Moonlight (구르미 그린 달빛) is the record most fans ask about. In episode 1, the crown prince played by Park Bo-gum pretends to study in Yeongjugak, the small pavilion on the garden's Bongnae island, while his father the king walks past. In episode 5, Princess Myeongeun (Jung Hye-sung) invites Hong Ra-on (Kim Yoo-jung) for a boat ride on the pond, and Ra-on ends up falling into the water while the crown prince watches.

The Red Sleeve (옷소매 붉은 끝동) uses the garden as part of the palace; in episode 3, Crown Prince Yi San (Lee Jun-ho) and Deok-im (Lee Se-young) meet in a scene set up by Princess Cheongyeon. In Rookie Historian Goo Hae-ryung (신입사관 구해령), episode 1 shows Prince Yi Rim (Cha Eun-woo) crossing the bridge. In The King's Affection (연모), episode 4 has Crown Prince Lee Hwi (Park Eun-bin) crossing a bridge with attendants while new guard Kim Ga-on (Choi Byung-chan) breaks the rule of walking five steps behind.

Moon Lovers: Scarlet Heart Ryeo (달의 연인 - 보보경심 려) filmed an episode 4 scene on a bridge here after Hae-soo (IU) is rescued, an almost-kiss that gets interrupted. 100 Days My Prince (백일의 낭군님) used Gwanghallu, Ojakgyo and Wanwoljeong as the palace garden where the main characters meet and talk. Queen: Love and War (간택 - 여인들의 전쟁) sends the queen candidates across Ojakgyo in episode 1, and in episode 11 the king and Kang Eun-bo (Jin Se-yeon) share a kiss on Bongnae island.

The dataset also lists Jang Ok-jung, Living by Love (장옥정, 사랑에 살다), with royal bride-selection scenes at Wanwoljeong in episodes 3 and 4; Rooftop Prince (옥탑방 왕세자), whose Joseon flashbacks place the crown princess's drowning at the garden's pond; Lovers of the Red Sky (홍천기), where a ritual in episode 1 takes place here; The Slave Hunters (추노); and the classic anthology Hometown Legends (전설의 고향), which uses Ojakgyo in its final scene.

Not every record is a costume drama. In My Roommate Is a Gumiho (간 떨어지는 동거), episode 1, Lee Dam (Hyeri) and her friend visit for a school project, put on hanbok and sit on the bridge in front of Gwanghallu acting out a historical drama scene. In Record of Youth (청춘기록), episode 9, Sa Hye-jun (Park Bo-gum) is shown filming a drama here. Delightful Girl Choon-hyang (쾌걸 춘향), a modern retelling of the Chunhyang story, stages the first meeting of Chun-hyang (Han Chae-young) and Mong-ryong (Jae Hee) here in episode 1.

The only film in the records is Masquerade (광해, 2012), with the scene where Lee Byung-hun reads a poem to Han Hyo-joo. For K-pop fans, VICTON filmed the opening of episode 11 (North Jeolla) of the travel show Tour Avatar here.

sections.heading: Walking the Garden: Gwanghallu, Ojakgyo, Wanwoljeong and Wolmae's House
paragraphs: The garden is flat and compact, and a relaxed loop takes about an hour, or 90 minutes with photos. After the ticket gate, follow the path to the pond and you will see the main sights in this order.

The pavilion stands on tall stone pillars beside the pond. Visitors are generally not allowed up on the floor, so the classic photo is from the pond edge in front of it, framing the roof and its reflection. This is the angle you will recognize from many palace scenes.

The long stone bridge with four arches is named after the bridge of magpies in the Korean legend of Gyeonu and Jiknyeo, two lovers who can meet only once a year. Walking across it is said to bring luck in love, which is why couples in dramas keep ending up on it. Large koi gather under the bridge; you can usually buy fish food near the pond.

Wanwoljeong, the colorful pavilion standing in the water, is the moon-viewing pavilion where the dataset places the bride-selection scenes. The small islands in the pond represent the mythical mountains where immortals were believed to live; Bongnae island with Yeongjugak is where Park Bo-gum's crown prince "studies" in Love in the Moonlight.

Toward the back of the garden is a shrine with a portrait of Chunhyang, and Wolmae's House (월매집), a group of thatched-roof buildings recreating the home of Chunhyang's mother. It is the quietest corner and a good place for traditional hanok photos without the crowds at the pond.

sections.heading: Address, Hours and How to Get There
paragraphs: Show the driver 광한루원 or the address 전북특별자치도 남원시 요천로 1447. The KCISA data lists it under the older province name 전라북도 남원시 요천로 1447; both work in Naver Map, KakaoMap and Kakao T.

According to the public data, the garden is open every day of the year, 8am to 7pm in summer and 8am to 6pm in winter. After the paid hours it stays open free of charge for two more hours (until 9pm in summer and 8pm in winter), when the pavilions are lit. There is an admission fee during the day; confirm the current price on the Namwon City tourism site or at the gate. Phone: 063-625-4861.

Namwon Station (남원역) is on the KTX Jeolla Line toward Yeosu. From Yongsan Station the ride usually takes around two to two and a half hours depending on the train. From Namwon Station, a taxi to Gwanghallu Garden takes roughly 10 minutes; local city buses also run toward downtown, but a taxi is simpler on a day trip.

Buses run from Seoul and other cities to the Namwon bus terminals in the center of town. From there the garden is close enough to walk in about 15 to 20 minutes, or it is a very short taxi ride. Check the terminal name on your ticket and type 광한루원 into Naver Map or KakaoMap for walking directions; Google Maps does not give full walking directions in Korea.

sections.heading: Where to Eat Near Gwanghallu Garden
paragraphs: Namwon is best known in Korea for chueotang (추어탕), a thick, peppery loach soup, and many restaurants around the garden specialize in it. If you want something milder, order it with rice and add perilla powder and chopped chili to taste.

The KCISA dataset also lists several TV-featured restaurants in Namwon. Gyeongbangnu (경방루, 남원시 광한북로 29), just north of the garden, appeared on Baek Jong-won's Top 3 Chef King (백종원의 3대천왕) for its long-running sweet and sour pork. Baktorang (박토랑, 남원시 광한서로 50), on the west side, was featured on Korean Table (한국인의 밥상) for gourd and perilla dishes. In the town center, the bakery Myeongmun Jegwa (명문제과, 남원시 용성로 56) was on Top 3 Chef King for its cream soboro bread, an easy snack for the train home. Hours change, so check Naver Map before you go.

sections.heading: Visit Tips: Best Time, Photos and Etiquette
paragraphs: Go early or go late. Mornings right after 8am are calm and the light on the pavilion is soft. On the other end, staying for the free evening hours lets you see Gwanghallu and Ojakgyo lit up and reflected in the pond, as in the photo above.

Seasons. Spring brings blossoms and the Chunhyang Festival (춘향제), Namwon's biggest event, usually held around May, when the garden is busiest. Autumn color and still winter mornings are quieter. In summer, bring water and a hat; there is shade under the old trees but the paths get hot.

Hanbok photos. Like the characters in My Roommate Is a Gumiho, many visitors wear hanbok here. Rental shops operate near the garden; prices and hours vary, so search 남원 한복대여 on Naver Map. Do not climb on stone walls or lean over the pond for a shot.

Respect the heritage. Gwanghallu is a national Treasure. Follow the signs on where you may walk, keep tripods out of the main paths when it is crowded, and do not feed the fish anything other than the food sold on site.

Make it a day trip. If you have extra time, the KCISA data lists other Namwon filming spots outside the garden, such as Namwon Land (남원랜드) in Youth of May and the old Seodo Station film site (구서도역 영상촬영장) in Mr. Sunshine. They need a taxi, so treat them as separate stops.

sections.heading: Why Saha-gu Belongs on Your Busan Screen Trip
paragraphs: Saha-gu is the far western end of Busan, where the city's hills drop to the mouth of the Nakdong River and the open sea. It packs three very different landscapes into one district: the painted hillside lanes of Gamcheon Culture Village, the wide tidal flats of Dadaepo Beach and the forested headland of Molundae, and the reed beds and bird sanctuary of Eulsukdo. All three are reachable from Busan Metro Line 1, which ends at Dadaepo Beach Station.

Korea's public KCISA filming-location dataset (한국문화정보원 미디어 촬영지 데이터) lists 21 records with a Saha-gu address. Gamcheon Culture Village appears five times: as the neighborhood where Jung Kyung-ho's detective lodges in Life on Mars, the home of Kim Rae-won's Ji-o in Luca: The Beginning, and the place where Esom's Lee Young-jae grew up with her brother in The Third Charm, plus K-pop visits by THE BOYZ and fromis_9. Dadaepo Beach is where Lee Min-ho's King Lee Gon gallops his horse Maximus in episode 1 of The King: Eternal Monarch, and the Eulsukdo estuary shows up in Life on Mars, Money Flower and the film Will You Be There? The rest of the list is local TV food.

sections.heading: Gamcheon Culture Village: Life on Mars, Luca and The Third Charm
paragraphs: Gamcheon Culture Village (감천문화마을) grew from a hillside settlement built by refugees during the Korean War. The small houses were laid out in terraces so that each one keeps a view of the valley, and since an arts project began here around 2009 the walls, stairways and rooftops have filled with murals, sculptures and small galleries.

In the dataset, Life on Mars uses the village as the background of the lodging where Jung Kyung-ho's detective stays after he wakes up in 1988. In Luca: The Beginning, Gamcheon is where Kim Rae-won's Ji-o lives, and episode 1 has him chased through its narrow alleys. The Third Charm sets the teenage and twenty-something years of Lee Young-jae (Esom) and her brother Soo-jae (Yang Dong-geun) here. On the K-pop side, THE BOYZ members Kevin, New and Juhaknyeon visited on a Busan trip, and fromis_9's Jiwon and Chaeyoung came looking for murals on their own Busan tour.

Start at the information center near the main entrance, pick up a village map, and follow the painted fish and arrows along the main lane. Popular stops include the Little Prince statue looking over the valley. The dataset lists visiting hours of 9am to 6pm in summer and 9am to 5pm in winter. This is still a residential neighborhood, so keep your voice down, stay on the public lanes and never photograph into windows or open doors.

Take Busan Metro Line 1 to Toseong Station (토성역), leave by exit 6, and ride a small village bus (Saha-gu 1-1, 2 or 2-2) uphill to the Gamcheon Culture Village stop; the ride takes about 10 minutes. A taxi from Toseong or Nampo takes 10 to 15 minutes. For the driver, show 감천문화마을 or 부산광역시 사하구 감내2로 203. The village is steep, so many visitors ride up and walk down.

sections.heading: Dadaepo Beach: The King: Eternal Monarch and the Sunset Fountain
paragraphs: Dadaepo Beach (다대포해수욕장) sits where the Nakdong River meets the sea, so the beach is wide, shallow and very flat. At low tide the wet sand turns into a mirror for the sky, which is why it is best known as a sunset spot. That mirror-like sand is also what made it a natural choice for episode 1 of The King: Eternal Monarch, where Lee Min-ho's King Lee Gon rides his white horse Maximus along the shore. The dataset also records BTS member Jimin filming a V Live broadcast here on a trip home to Busan, and SF9's Chani, Dawon and Inseong visiting on Battle Trip.

Right behind the beach is the Dadaepo Sunset Fountain of Dreams (다대포 꿈의 낙조분수), a large round music fountain with lights and water jets set to songs in the evening. It runs seasonally, usually in the warmer months, and shows can be cancelled for weather, so check the Saha-gu or Visit Busan schedule before planning around it. In late autumn the beach itself is the show: bring a jacket and walk out on the sand at golden hour.
Next to the beach, the Dadaepo Gouni Eco Trail (고우니생태길) is a flat wooden boardwalk over the coastal wetland, good when the wind is strong on the open sand.

Ride Line 1 to its last stop, Dadaepo Beach Station (다대포해수욕장역). The beach and fountain are a few minutes' walk from the station exits. From Nampo Station the ride takes about 30 minutes. By taxi, show 다대포해수욕장 or 부산광역시 사하구 몰운대1길 14.

sections.heading: Molundae and Jangnim Port: Cliffs, Pines and a Fishing Harbor
paragraphs: At the southern end of Dadaepo Beach, Molundae (몰운대) is a pine-covered headland that pushes out into the sea. Its name is often explained as a cliff that disappears into clouds and fog, and it is designated a Busan Metropolitan City Monument (No. 27). A loop of forest trails leads to cliffs of layered sedimentary rock called the Dadaepo Formation, with views of small islands offshore.

Molundae does not appear in the KCISA filming dataset, so treat it as the scenic extension of the Dadaepo filming spot rather than a drama location. The walk from the beach to the end of the headland and back takes about one to one and a half hours at an easy pace. Wear shoes with grip, because the rocks near the water can be slippery, and stay behind the safety lines on the cliffs. For a taxi, show 몰운대 or 부산광역시 사하구 다대동 산144.

Between Hadan and Dadaepo, Jangnim Port (장림포구, 장림로93번길 72) is a small fishing harbor whose brightly painted buildings along the water have earned it the nickname of Busan's little Venice. In the dataset it is where NCT's Jaemin and Jeno stopped during their Busan trip on Battle Trip. Jangnim Station on Line 1 is the closest stop, followed by a short taxi or a walk of about 20 minutes.

sections.heading: Eulsukdo and the Nakdong River Estuary: Life on Mars and Money Flower
paragraphs: Eulsukdo (을숙도) is a low island at the mouth of the Nakdong River, and the estuary around it is one of Korea's best-known stopovers for migratory birds. November through February is the main season for wintering ducks, swans and other water birds, so this trip timing works well. The Nakdong Estuary Eco Center (낙동강하구에코센터, 낙동남로 1240) has exhibits, observation windows and telescopes over the wetland; the dataset lists it as open Tuesday to Sunday from 9am to 6pm and closed on Mondays.

The reed beds here have a strong screen history. In the dataset, Life on Mars uses the estuary as the scene where a village chief is found murdered, with the tall reeds as backdrop. In episode 1 of Money Flower, Park Se-young's character Na Mo-hyeon works as a guide in the bird sanctuary on Eulsukdo. In the 2016 film Will You Be There?, the eco center is where Tae-ho goes to find Yeon-ah after reading Soo-hyun's letter.
Take Line 1 to Hadan Station (하단역), then a city bus across the Nakdong River bridge toward Eulsukdo, or a taxi of about 10 minutes. For the driver, show 낙동강하구에코센터 or 부산광역시 사하구 낙동남로 1240.

sections.heading: Where to Eat in Saha-gu: TV-Famous Local Restaurants
paragraphs: Saha-gu's TV food picks are neighborhood places with Korean-only menus. Yeongjin Dwaeji Gukbap (영진돼지국밥 본점, 하신번영로157번길 39) is the pork-and-rice soup house that Day6's Sungjin recommended; the dataset lists it as open 9:30am to 9:30pm but also marks Sunday as a closing day, so check before going. Bokseong Banjeom (복성반점, 하신중앙로 289) is the spicy seafood jjamppong noodle shop from episode 9 of Baek Jong-won's Top 3 Chef King, open 11am to 9pm and closed on Tuesdays.

For seafood, Namhae Dalin Hoetjip (남해달인횟집, 사리로 40) serves raw-fish set meals featured on Morning Wide, Live Today Morning and VJ Special Forces, and opens Tuesday to Sunday from noon. Naekigo (내키고, 낙동대로563번안길 35-1) specializes in grilled and raw mackerel from Live Tonight and opens in the evening. Song Bujang Yeontan Galbi (송부장연탄갈비, 하신번영로167번길 6) from The Master of Living grills beef ribs from 5pm, Monday to Saturday. For dessert and coffee, small cafes with rooftop seating line the main lane of Gamcheon Culture Village.

sections.heading: A Half-Day Saha-gu Itinerary
paragraphs: Begin at Toseong Station around 10am and ride the village bus up to Gamcheon Culture Village. Spend about two hours on the lanes and viewpoints, then walk or ride back down. Take Line 1 west for a pork soup or jjamppong lunch near Hadan or Sinpyeong. In the early afternoon, visit the Nakdong Estuary Eco Center on Eulsukdo for the birds and reed beds (skip this on Mondays). Continue by Line 1 to Dadaepo Beach Station, walk the Molundae trail in the late afternoon, and finish on the sand at Dadaepo for sunset. Allow six to seven hours in total.

If you only have a few hours, choose Gamcheon in the morning and Dadaepo at sunset; both are on Line 1 and about 30 minutes apart. Check opening hours on Naver Map or KakaoMap before you go, because the dataset times may have changed, and remember that the fountain shows are seasonal.

sections.heading: Why Yeongdo and Songdo Belong on Your Busan Screen Trip
paragraphs: Most visitors see Busan from Haeundae or Gwangalli, but the island district of Yeongdo-gu and the Songdo coast in neighboring Seo-gu show a different side of the city: steep hillside lanes, a working harbor, sea cliffs and Korea's first public beach. Both sit just across the water from the old downtown of Nampo-dong, so they pair naturally with a Jung-gu day.

Korea's public KCISA filming-location dataset (한국문화정보원 미디어 촬영지 데이터) lists 24 records with a Yeongdo-gu address and 12 in Seo-gu. They mix a few strong screen locations with a long list of TV food picks. The film The Attorney recreated the 1980s at Huinnyeoul Culture Village, the drama Life on Mars turned the National Maritime Museum into a Seoul police headquarters, The King: Eternal Monarch filmed at Chungmu-dong Dawn Market, and Shopping King Louie used a terrace on Cheonmasan. Kang Daniel, who grew up in Busan, recommended Huinnyeoul, Taejongdae and Yeongdo Bridge for a Yeongdo tour, and Infinite Challenge, THE BOYZ, NCT, SF9 and 2 Days & 1 Night all appear too.

sections.heading: Huinnyeoul Culture Village: The Attorney and Infinite Challenge
paragraphs: Huinnyeoul Culture Village (흰여울문화마을) is a row of small houses painted white and pastel, stacked along a cliff above the outer anchorage of Busan port. The name means a stream that runs white like snow, after the water that once ran down the slope into the sea. In the dataset it is the location where The Attorney recreated 1980s Busan, where Infinite Challenge episode 459 sent the cast to find disguise clothes, and where THE BOYZ members Sangyeon, Younghoon and Eric carried out a mission.

The main lane, Huinnyeoul-gil, is lined with small cafes and viewpoints over the ships waiting offshore. Below it, the Jeoryeong coastal path (절영해안산책로) runs along the water and ends at a short tunnel that is a favorite photo spot. Remember that this is a residential village: people live behind those doors, so keep your voice down and avoid photographing into homes.

There is no subway on Yeongdo. From Nampo Station (Line 1), cross to the bus stops on the Yeongdo Bridge side and take a city bus to the Huinnyeoul Culture Village (흰여울문화마을) stop on Jeoryeong-ro; KakaoMap shows the current routes. A taxi from Nampo takes about 10 minutes. For the driver, show 흰여울문화마을 or 부산광역시 영도구 영선동4가 605-3.

sections.heading: Yeongdo Bridge and the Yeongdo Food Picks
paragraphs: Yeongdo Bridge (영도대교) links Nampo-dong to the island. It is a drawbridge, and according to the dataset its span is raised once a day from 2:00pm to 2:15pm. That daily lift is one of the stops Kang Daniel picked for his Yeongdo tour. Watch from the Nampo-dong side or from the Yeongdo end at Daegyo-dong, and arrive a little early because the crowd builds before two.

Yeongdo has a strong local food list in the dataset. Dalttne (달뜨네, 절영로 205) serves mackerel sashimi and sirak gukbap and appears on Battle Trip and Korean Table; Kang Daniel also ate here with a teacher from his old school. It opens Wednesday to Monday from 5pm to 10pm. Jaegi Dwaeji Gukbap (재기돼지국밥, 절영로49번길 25) is a pork soup house from Baek Jong-won's Top 3 Chef King, open daily from 8am. Kang Daniel's favorite tteokbokki is at Donald Tteokbokki (도날드 떡볶이, 남항새싹길 9), open Monday to Saturday. For something sweet, Imodonas (이모도나스, 절영로 134) sells donuts and croquettes from Live Today Morning.

Drama fans should look for Yang Dabang (양다방, 대평로 49), a retro coffee house where Jung Kyung-ho and Go Ah-sung investigate the "Yang Dabang murder" in Life on Mars. The dataset lists it as open Monday to Saturday from 7:30am to 6pm and Sunday from 9am.

sections.heading: Taejongdae and the National Maritime Museum
paragraphs: Taejongdae (태종대, 전망로 24) is the park at the southern tip of Yeongdo, with pine forest, sea cliffs and views toward Japan's Tsushima on clear days. It is another of Kang Daniel's picks. The loop road inside the park is closed to private cars, so walk it or ride the Danubi tour train, which stops at the observatory, the lighthouse and Taejong Temple. The dataset lists the park as open from 4am in summer and 5am in winter until midnight.

Near the park entrance, Taejongdae Sarangbang (태종대 사랑방 조개구이, 태종로 816 2층) is the grilled clam restaurant where NCT's Jaemin and Jeno ate on Battle Trip, also featured on Food Road. On the coast nearby, Chungbukjip Nunaya (충북집 누나야, 감지해변길 90) at Gamji Beach is the seafood tent Lee Seung-gi visited with baseball star Lee Dae-ho on 2 Days & 1 Night.

The National Maritime Museum (국립해양박물관, 해양로301번길 45) sits on the harbor side of Yeongdo. In Life on Mars it stood in for the Seoul Metropolitan Police headquarters. Inside are ship models, an aquarium tunnel and a children's area. The dataset lists it as open Tuesday to Friday from 9am to 6pm and to 7pm on weekends, closed Mondays.

City buses run from Nampo Station to the Taejongdae bus stop in about 25 to 30 minutes; check KakaoMap for the current route. The museum is a short taxi ride from Taejongdae. For a taxi, show 태종대 or 부산광역시 영도구 전망로 24.

sections.heading: Songdo, Seo-gu: Cable Car, Skywalk and Dawn Market
paragraphs: Across the harbor mouth, Songdo Beach in Seo-gu opened in 1913 as Korea's first public beach. Today its draws are the Songdo Marine Cable Car, which carries cabins over the bay, and the Songdo Cloud Trail (송도구름산책로), a curved skywalk with glass panels over the water. In the dataset, SF9's Chani, Dawon and Inseong rode the cable car on Battle Trip, and it is listed as open daily from 9am to 9pm. NCT filmed a segment at Cafe Haein (카페 해인, 암남로94번길 62), a sea-view cafe open daily from 11:30am to 11pm.

For seafood, Samyeong Hoetjip (삼영횟집, 송도해변로 83-1) is the cold raw-fish soup place from 6 O'Clock My Hometown. Inland, Yeongnam Naengmyeon Milmyeon (영남냉면밀면, 보수대로201번길 7) serves Busan's signature cold wheat noodles from Battle Trip episode 13.

Chungmu-dong Dawn Market (충무동 새벽시장, 해안새벽시장길 68) is the harbor market where Prime Minister Koo Seo-ryung, played by Jung Eun-chae, arrives with her entourage in episode 3 of The King: Eternal Monarch. Come early in the morning to see it at its busiest. Up on Cheonmasan, Cheonmasan Eco House (천마산에코하우스, 천마산로 342) is the guesthouse terrace where Oh Dae-hwan's character invites Lim Se-mi's in Shopping King Louie episode 12; it is also a stay, so treat it as a viewpoint unless you book a room.
A taxi from Jagalchi or Nampo Station to Songdo Beach takes about 10 minutes. Several city buses also run there from Nampo. Show 송도해수욕장 or 송도해상케이블카 to the driver.

sections.heading: A Half-Day Yeongdo and Songdo Itinerary
paragraphs: Start at Nampo Station around 1:30pm and walk to Yeongdo Bridge for the 2pm lift. Cross to Yeongdo, then take a short taxi or bus to Huinnyeoul Culture Village and spend an hour on the lane and the coastal path. Continue to Taejongdae by bus or taxi and ride the Danubi train for sunset views. Finish with grilled clams near the park entrance, or with mackerel sashimi at Dalttne when it opens at 5pm. Allow about five to six hours.

If you prefer mornings, reverse the plan: begin at Chungmu-dong Dawn Market, ride the Songdo cable car, walk the skywalk, then cross to Yeongdo for lunch and Huinnyeoul. Hills on Yeongdo are steep, so wear good shoes, and check opening hours on Naver Map or KakaoMap before you go, because the dataset times may have changed.

sections.heading: Why Busan Jung-gu Is the Old-Downtown Screen Set
paragraphs: Before Haeundae's towers and Gwangalli's bridge, Busan's downtown was Jung-gu, the small harbor district around Nampo-dong, Gwangbok-dong and Bupyeong-dong. It is where the city's markets, cinemas and port grew up, and it still feels dense, busy and very Busan. Korea's public KCISA filming-location dataset lists 76 records with a Jung-gu address: 52 from variety and food shows, 15 from idol and artist visits, 5 from films and 4 from TV dramas.

The screen highlights are compact. Bosu-dong Book Street leads with 6 records, including the films The Attorney and The King and the dramas Shopping King Louie. Hwaguk Banjeom, a Chinese restaurant, appears in Confidential Assignment, The King: Eternal Monarch and Omniscient Interfering View. The Commodore Hotel Busan stood in for a Pyongyang hotel in Crash Landing on You. Almost everything else is food: Jung-gu is the most food-show-heavy district we have covered, with fish cake shops, milmyeon noodle houses and market stalls that Baek Jong-won, Running Man and Wednesday Food Talk all visited.
Everything in this guide sits within roughly a 20 minute walk of Nampo and Jagalchi stations on Busan Metro Line 1, so it is an easy half day with no transfers.

sections.heading: Bosu-dong Book Street: The Attorney, The King and Shopping King Louie
paragraphs: Bosu-dong Book Street (보수동 책방골목, 부산광역시 중구 대청로 67-1) is a narrow lane of second-hand bookshops with books stacked floor to ceiling, a market that started after the Korean War. In The Attorney, Song Kang-ho's character comes back here to buy back the bar-exam books he once sold to a used bookstore. In the opening of the film The King, Jo In-sung runs through the alley, and in episode 8 of Shopping King Louie, Louie (Seo In-guk) and Go Bok-sil (Nam Ji-hyun) share their kiss in the bookshop lane, right after Bok-sil discovers that Louie can read Japanese, French, German and Spanish as he flips through books.

The alley also turns up in dating show Heart Signal, where Oh Young-ju and Lee Kyu-bin gave each other books here, and in visits by Girl's Day's Minah and three members of THE BOYZ (Jacob, Hyunjae and Juyeon). The dataset lists the lane as open around the clock, but most shops keep daytime hours and many close on Sundays, so visit on a weekday afternoon.
From Jagalchi Station (Line 1), walk north across Gukje Market and Bupyeong Market, about 12 to 15 minutes. For a taxi, show 보수동 책방골목 or 대청로 67-1.

sections.heading: Gukje Market and Kkangtong Market: Running Man, Taeyang and Fish Cake Alley
paragraphs: Gukje Market (국제시장, 국제시장 2길 25) is the sprawling covered market that gave the 2014 film Ode to My Father its Korean title. In the dataset, Running Man episode 421 staged a surprise chase through its lanes, fromis_9's Jiwon and Chaeyoung did a market food tour here, and Taeyang visited Kkotbunine (꽃분이네, 중구로 42), the small goods shop made famous by that film. The market runs daily from 9am to 8pm and closes on the 1st and 3rd Monday.

Just to the north, Bupyeong Kkangtong Market (부평깡통시장, 부평1길 48) is where Taeyang ate street food on TV. Its lanes are the fish cake capital of the district: VJ Special Forces visited more than ten eomuk shops here, including Hwangong Eomuk (환공어묵, 중구로43번길 25) and Hyoseong Eomuk (효성어묵 부평점, 중구로43번길 39), both open from early morning. Igane Tteokbokki (이가네떡볶이, 부평1길 48) appears on both Baek Jong-won's Top 3 Chef King and VJ Special Forces, open Monday to Saturday until 5pm.

The night market (야시장) opens daily from 7:30pm to 11:30pm, according to the dataset. Nearby, Wonjo Kkangtong Golmok Bibim Dangmyeon (원조 깡통골목 비빔당면, 중구로47번길 28), a spicy cold glass-noodle stall, has been on Top 3 Chef King, Live Today Morning and Korean Table. Gukje Tongdak (국제통닭 부평본점, 중구로 47번길 33-1) is the fried chicken shop fromis_9's Saerom visited in her Busan vlog.
Use Jagalchi Station (Line 1) Exit 7 for Gukje Market, about a 5 minute walk; Kkangtong Market is a further 5 minutes north.

sections.heading: BIFF Square and Gwangbok-ro: The King: Eternal Monarch and Street Snacks
paragraphs: BIFF Square (BIFF광장) is the cinema street that hosted the first Busan International Film Festival, with celebrity handprints set into the pavement. It is also the best place to try ssiat hotteok, a sweet pancake filled with seeds and nuts. Nampo-dong Wonjo Chapssal Hotteok (남포동 원조 찹쌀호떡 본점, 비프광장로 36), featured on Live Today Morning, opens daily from 10am to 9pm.

A block east, the Gwangbok-ro fashion street (광복로 패션거리) is where Kang Shin-jae walks along with an ice cream in The King: Eternal Monarch. For a sit-down meal, Wonsan Myeonok (원산면옥, 광복로 56-8) is a Hamheung-style naengmyeon house praised on Wednesday Food Talk, and Ilmi Danpatjuk (일미단팥죽, 광복로49번길 11) serves sweet red-bean porridge from Top 3 Chef King. Kang Daniel recommended Nampo Sujebi (남포수제비, 광복로49번길 7-1) for hand-torn noodle soup and Ijaemo Pizza (이재모피자, 광복중앙로 31), a local pizza institution closed on Sundays.
Nampo Station (Line 1) Exit 1 or Jagalchi Station Exit 7 both put you within a 3 minute walk.

sections.heading: Jagalchi Market, Hwaguk Banjeom and the Commodore Hotel
paragraphs: Jagalchi Market (자갈치시장, 자갈치해안로 52) is Korea's best-known fish market, facing the harbor. In 2 Days & 1 Night season 1 the cast helped out by delivering ice here, and April filmed an episode of their web show at the market. Buy seafood downstairs and have it prepared upstairs, or try a dataset pick: Baekhwa Yanggopchang 1-ho (백화양곱창1호, 자갈치로 23) for grilled beef tripe, Gimhae Sikdang (김해식당, 자갈치로 51-2) for monkfish, and Juyeonne Gomjangeo (주연네곰장어, 자갈치해안로 61) for grilled hagfish from Battle Trip. The market is open daily from 5am to 10pm, closing on the 1st and 3rd Tuesday.

Hwaguk Banjeom (화국반점, 백산길 3) is the Chinese restaurant where Hyun Bin jumps out of a window in Confidential Assignment, and where Myeong-ho's birthday party is held in The King: Eternal Monarch. Omniscient Interfering View episode 22 ordered its fried shrimp and ganjjajang. It opens daily from 11:30am to 9:30pm, closing on the 1st and 3rd Monday.

The Commodore Hotel Busan (코모도호텔 부산, 중구로 151), with its traditional palace-style roof, played the upscale Pyongyang hotel the "Dooly couple" visit in Crash Landing on You, and was a main setting of the film Real. It sits on the hill above Jungang Station (Line 1), a short taxi ride from Nampo.

sections.heading: A Half-Day Jung-gu Itinerary
paragraphs: Start around 11am at Jagalchi Market for a seafood lunch, then walk to BIFF Square for a seed hotteok and look for the handprints. Cross Gwangbok-ro, then head north into Gukje Market and Kkangtong Market for fish cake tasting. Continue uphill to Bosu-dong Book Street for an hour of browsing in the afternoon light. If you still have energy, take a short taxi to Hwaguk Banjeom for an early dinner, or come back to Kkangtong for the night market at 7:30pm. Allow about five to six hours.

Jung-gu is crowded on weekends, and many small shops close on Sundays or on specific Mondays and Tuesdays, so check hours on Naver Map or KakaoMap before you go. If you stay longer, Busan Tower in Yongdusan Park and Gamcheon Culture Village are a short taxi ride away.

sections.heading: Why Suyeong-gu Is Busan's Bridge-and-Beach Screen Set
paragraphs: If Haeundae is Busan's postcard, Suyeong-gu is the view that directors cut to when a story needs to say "we are in Busan now." The district wraps around Gwangalli Beach, a curve of sand about 1.4 km long facing Gwangan Bridge, the double-deck suspension bridge that crosses the bay toward Haeundae. Korea's public KCISA filming-location dataset lists 39 records with a Suyeong-gu address: 15 from idol and artist visits, 15 from variety and food shows, 8 from TV dramas and 1 from a film. Two places do most of the work: Gwangalli Beach appears in 13 records and Gwangan Bridge in 10.

That concentration makes Suyeong-gu one of the easiest filming areas in Korea to visit. Busan Metro Line 2 runs right behind the beach, with Geumnyeonsan, Gwangan and Suyeong stations all within walking distance of the sand, and most food spots in the dataset sit within a few blocks of the promenade. You can see almost everything in a single afternoon and evening.

sections.heading: Gwangalli Beach: Dance Sports Girls, Shopping King Louie and Let's Eat 3
paragraphs: Gwangalli Beach (광안리해수욕장, 부산광역시 수영구 광안해변로 219) is open around the clock, with official swimming in July and August. In episode 11 of Dance Sports Girls, the high-school dance team takes a trip here and poses for a group photo at the far eastern end of the beach; that evening their two teachers drink on the sand and one asks the other to take over the club. In episode 5 of Shopping King Louie, Go Bok-sil, Louie and Jo In-sung arrive at the beach on their Busan trip, and Let's Eat 3 also shot scenes on the sand and against the bridge.

The 2016 film Will You Be There? uses Gwangalli to show the lasting friendship between the present-day Soo-hyun and Tae-ho. For K-pop fans, the dataset records SEVENTEEN filming their 'Adore U' part-switch video here, Stray Kids' Seungmin posting the beach on Instagram, and visits by Taeyang, fromis_9's Jiwon and Chaeyoung, Block B's Jaehyo and ATEEZ.
Take Line 2 to Gwangan Station and use Exit 3 or 5; it is about a 7 minute walk downhill to the beach. For a taxi, show the driver 광안리해수욕장 or the address 광안해변로 219.

sections.heading: Gwangan Bridge: D.P., Sisyphus and Music Video Night Views
paragraphs: Gwangan Bridge (광안대교) is the single most-filmed structure in the district. In episode 3 of D.P., An Jun-ho and Han Ho-yeol arrive in Busan and ride a Busan City Tour bus across it. In episode 3 of Sisyphus: The Myth, Kang Seo-hae crosses the bridge in a taxi. In episode 1 of Now, We Are Breaking Up, Hwang Chi-sook drives over it on the way to call her model boyfriend, and in episode 1 of Fates & Furies, Goo Hae-ra brings an Italian businessman here.
The bridge is also a music video favorite. Apink's 'Remember' and BTOB's 'It's Okay Without You' (너 없인 안 된다) both used it, and BTS's Jimin posted a finger-heart photo with the bridge on Twitter.

The classic view is from the middle of Gwangalli Beach after sunset, when the bridge lights change color. For a lower, quieter angle, walk north to Millak Waterside Park (민락수변공원) at the eastern end of the beach, where the bridge passes close overhead. Busan City Tour buses on some routes cross the upper deck, which is the easiest way to recreate the D.P. ride without a car. The Busan Fireworks Festival is also held over this bay each autumn; check the official date before you plan around it.

sections.heading: Busking, Pizza and Raw Fish on the Promenade
paragraphs: Gwangalli's promenade is one of Busan's main busking stages, and on clear weekend evenings you will usually find singers set up facing the bridge. Food in the dataset is clustered here too. Mad Dogs (매드독스, 광안해변로 235), a Chicago-style deep-dish pizza place right on the beachfront, appears in Baek Jong-won's Top 3 Chef King, Delicious Rendezvous and Siksin Namnyeo, and NU'EST's Ren visited; the dataset lists it as open daily from noon to midnight.

For something more local, Gaemijip Gwangalli (개미집 광안리직영점, 광남로130번길 9), the nakji-bokkeum (spicy stir-fried octopus) chain Simon Dominic recommended on Wednesday Food Talk, opens daily from 11am to 10pm. Toward Millak, Pungseong Galbi & Jogaegui (풍성갈비&조개구이, 민락수변로 7) serves grilled shellfish from 4pm to midnight. Millak's raw fish market buildings sit beside the waterside park if you want sashimi with a bridge view.

sections.heading: Namcheon-dong and F1963: Squid Tempura, Bingsu and a Wire Factory
paragraphs: West of the beach, Namcheon-dong is a quieter residential neighborhood known for its cherry-blossom apartment roads in spring. The dataset lists Dari-jip (다리집 본점, 남천바다로10번길 70), a squid tempura and tteokbokki shop visited by Son Dam-bi, open Wednesday to Monday, and Namcheon Green Tea Patbingsu (남천녹차팥빙수, 수영로394번길 28), featured on Live Today, for shaved ice. Namcheon Station on Line 2 is the closest stop.

North of Suyeong Station, F1963 (복합문화공간 F1963, 구락로123번길 20) is a former wire-rope factory turned into a culture complex with a bookstore, cafes, galleries and gardens. Hong Jin-ho and Lee Na-woo busked here together on Begin Again Korea. The dataset lists it as open daily from 9am to 9pm. The nearest subway stop is Mangmi Station on Line 3, about a 15 minute walk, so many visitors take a short taxi from Suyeong Station.

Nearby, Yeongjin Dwaeji Gukbap (영진돼지국밥 코스트코센텀점, 구락로 86) is where Running Man episode 328 ate pork-and-rice soup with TWICE, and Suyeong Dwaeji Gukbap (수영 돼지국밥, 무학로 6), recommended by NCT's Johnny on Wednesday Food Talk, opens from 8am.

sections.heading: Hwangnyeongsan and a Half-Day Suyeong-gu Itinerary
paragraphs: Hwangnyeongsan (황령산) rises on Suyeong-gu's western edge, and its summit area gives one of the widest night views of Busan, including Gwangan Bridge. Mugunghwa (무궁화, 황령산로8번길 5), a dumpling hot-pot restaurant with a signature from Shinhwa's Minwoo, sits at the foot of the mountain road. The summit is easiest by taxi.

A simple half day: start at F1963 around 2pm for coffee and the bookstore, take a taxi to Namcheon-dong for squid tempura at Dari-jip, then walk east along the beach from Geumnyeonsan Station toward Gwangan. Watch the sunset from the sand, eat pizza or grilled shellfish, and finish at Millak Waterside Park as the bridge lights come on. Allow about five hours. Restaurants change, so confirm hours on Naver Map or KakaoMap before you go.

sections.heading: Why Haeundae Is Busan's Biggest Screen Stage
paragraphs: Haeundae-gu is the district most travelers picture when they think of Busan: a 1.5 km curve of pale sand, a skyline of glass apartment towers, and a coastal road that winds east through fishing villages to a surf beach. Korea's public KCISA filming-location dataset lists 64 records with a Haeundae-gu address: 28 from variety and food shows, 24 from idol and artist visits, 10 from TV dramas and 2 from films. The single most-filmed drama is The King: Eternal Monarch, with five separate Haeundae locations.

What makes the district easy for fans is how compact it is. Busan Metro Line 2 runs along the coast through Centum City, Dongbaek and Haeundae stations, and the Donghae Line covers BEXCO and Songjeong. In one day you can walk the island where the drama placed its imperial palace, stand where Lee Min-ho fought outside the film festival theater, and finish on the beach from a K-pop music video.

sections.heading: Haeundae Beach and Gunam-ro: Seagulls, Street Food and a New Year Stroll
paragraphs: The beach itself (부산광역시 해운대구 우동) appears in the dataset for 1 Night 2 Days, for fromis_9 member Saerom's Busan travel vlog, and for We Got Married, where CNBLUE's Jung Yong-hwa fed snacks to seagulls. Get off at Haeundae Station on Line 2 and walk about 5 minutes down Gunam-ro (구남로), the wide pedestrian boulevard that leads straight to the sand.

The plaza along Gunam-ro is where, in episodes 9 and 10 of The King: Eternal Monarch, Lee Gon walks through Haeundae during the Lunar New Year. It is a pleasant, open space today, lined with busking spots and cafes. The side street Gunam-ro 41beon-gil is packed with spots from food shows like 6 O'Clock My Hometown, and Super Junior's Kyuhyun visited the tteokbokki shop Sanggugine (상국이네, 구남로41번길 40-1). Haeundae Traditional Market sits a block away for fish cakes and fried snacks.

sections.heading: Dongbaek Island and Marine City: The King's Imperial Palace
paragraphs: Walk west along the beach and you reach Dongbaek Island (동백섬, 부산광역시 해운대구 동백로 99), a small wooded headland now joined to the mainland. In The King: Eternal Monarch it is listed as the location of the imperial palace of the drama's Kingdom of Corea, and it also appears in episode 5 of Shopping King Louie, when Go Bok-sil travels to Busan, and in the dating show Heart Signal. A loop trail of about 1 km circles the island past pine trees, rocky coves, a lighthouse viewpoint and Nurimaru APEC House, the round summit hall built for the 2005 APEC meeting.

The trail is open all day and free. The closest subway stop is Dongbaek Station on Line 2; from Exit 1 it is about a 10 minute walk. Across the water is Marine City, the cluster of skyscrapers seen in many Busan night shots. The dataset lists Park Hyatt Busan (부산광역시 해운대구 마린시티1로 51) as the apartment with a private pool used by Chun Soo-ho in the drama Time.

sections.heading: Centum City: Busan Cinema Center, BEXCO and APEC Naru Park
paragraphs: Two Line 2 stops west of Dongbaek, Centum City is Busan's convention and culture district, and it holds four of The King's five Haeundae locations. Outside the Busan Cinema Center (영화의전당, 부산광역시 해운대구 수영강변대로 120), Lee Gon rides in with mounted guards and a SWAT team to rescue Jeong Tae-eul from Lee Lim's men. The building is the home of the Busan International Film Festival, and its giant cantilevered roof is lit with LED patterns after dark. It is open daily from 9am to 10pm.

The BEXCO convention complex (부산광역시 해운대구 APEC로 55) plays Busan CTX Station in episode 5 of The King, where Tae-eul heads for a high-speed train to Seoul, and it plays the PEXCO convention center hosting the Quantum Time conference in Sisyphus: The Myth. Right next door, the Busan Museum of Art (부산광역시 해운대구 APEC로 58) is a spot RM of BTS shared on Twitter; it opens Tuesday to Sunday, 10am to 6pm.

APEC Naru Park (부산광역시 해운대구 수영강변대로 93), a riverside lawn along the Suyeong River, is where Tae-eul spots the exhibition poster for Lee Gon. Nearby, the Im Kwon-taek Film Museum (센텀중앙로 55) is where Ha Moon-soo and Lee Kang-doo meet for their last date in Just Between Lovers; the dataset lists it as open Tuesday to Saturday, noon to 6pm.

sections.heading: Dalmaji-gil and Cheongsapo: BTS Views and Clam Grills
paragraphs: East of the beach, the road climbs onto Dalmaji Hill. Dalmaji-gil (달맞이길, 부산광역시 해운대구 달맞이길 190) is the road where BTS's V and actor Park Seo-joon stopped for photos, and the road Apink used in the music video for Hopefully Sky (하늘바라기), the solo debut of Apink's Jung Eun-ji. The hill is lined with cafes and galleries looking down on the sea. Near the bottom of the hill, Saeachim Sikdang (새아침식당, 달맞이길62번길 28) is the grilled-clam restaurant where Running Man episode 328 filmed and TWICE ate with the cast.

Over the hill, Cheongsapo (청사포) is a small fishing harbor with a red and white pair of lighthouses. The cafe Doré Doré Cheongsapo (도레도레 청사포점, 청사포로 137) was featured on Battle Trip, and Hajinine (하진이네, 청사포로 151), a late-night grilled-shellfish spot, appeared when Block B's Jaehyo visited. The easiest way here is the Haeundae Blue Line Park beach train, which runs along the old coastal rail line from Mipo near Haeundae Beach to Cheongsapo and Songjeong.

sections.heading: Songjeong Beach: Will You Be There and Apink's Music Video
paragraphs: Songjeong Beach (송정해수욕장, 부산광역시 해운대구 송정동 712-2) is quieter and shallower than Haeundae and is known as Busan's beginner surf beach, with board rental shops along the promenade. In the 2016 film Will You Be There?, it is the seaside where the younger Soo-hyun and Tae-ho talk 30 years in the past. The Hopefully Sky music video also filmed here and at the old, closed Songjeong Station building (송정중앙로6번길 60), a small heritage station a short walk inland.
Songjeong Station on the Donghae Line is about 10 minutes on foot from the sand, or ride the Blue Line beach train from Cheongsapo.

sections.heading: Half-Day Haeundae K-Drama Itinerary
paragraphs: Start at Centum City Station around 10am and walk past the Busan Cinema Center, the Busan Museum of Art and BEXCO, then cross to APEC Naru Park. Ride Line 2 two stops to Dongbaek, walk the island loop, and follow the beach east to Gunam-ro for lunch at Haeundae Market. In the afternoon, board the Blue Line Park beach train at Mipo, get off at Cheongsapo for coffee by the lighthouse, and continue to Songjeong for sunset on the beach. Allow five to six hours with stops.

For food, the dataset points to Busan staples: dwaeji gukbap (pork soup with rice) at Uiryeong Sikdang (의령식당, 우동1로50번길 15), visited by Dynamic Duo's Gaeko; cod soup at Haeundae Giwajip Daegutang (달맞이길104번길 46), where G-Dragon ate; and grilled clams on Dalmaji Hill. Restaurants change, so confirm hours on Naver Map or KakaoMap before you go.
